answer_1.quote: We focus on English‑Dutch translation, for which we can ensure good command for both languages. We train Transformer‑base models using Fairseq ... Our training data consists of a collection of MT corpora ... We compute SacreBLEU scores on the ‘devtest’ set ...

answer_2.quote: We compute SacreBLEU scores on the ‘devtest’ set ... In our tests for systematicity and substitutivity, we consider whether processing is local; ... We measure consistency as the equality of two translations after accounting for anticipated changes.

answer_4.quote: To address this question, we perform a manual analysis. We annotate 900 inconsistent translation pairs of the systematicity and substitutivity tests to establish whether the inconsistencies are benign or concerning.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators classify each inconsistent pair into one of four change types: (1) rephrasing, (2) different interpretations of source ambiguities, (3) error in one translation, (4) formatting differences. For substitutivity they also label synonym‑specific categories (incorrect translation, both incorrect differently, both correct differently, untranslated).
